parameters.Features: Overcurrent Protection;Short-Circuit  Protection;Overvoltage clamping protection;Under-voltage lockout;Thermal Protection;Overload protection

provenance.pins: datasheet p.5 Pin Functions (names, types) - EXCEPT pin 21, the PowerPAD, which the datasheet leaves unnumbered; 21 is the EasyEDA symbol's number for it, confirmed with tools/eda.py and p.6 Table 7.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings (vMax). Two groups and nothing between them: IN, P_IN, OUT, UVLO, FLT, PGOOD at 67 V; OVP, dVdT, IMON, MODE, SHDN, ILIM at 5.5 V. UVLO sitting in the 67 V group and OVP in the 5.5 V one is not an oddity - it is why UVLO must be the UPPER tap of the divider.
provenance.vMin: p.6 Recommended Operating Conditions: 4.5 V <= VIN <= 60 V

designVerdict: SELECTED as U10/U11, one per channel. 60 V / 6 A eFuse with an integrated FET.
notes: REPLACED an LM5069 (C52940995) driving a discrete NSS085N100S. The LM5069 needs 8 V to operate, so the LED output was dead below a 12 V contract and dead on a laptop port. This part works from 4.5 V, which was the requirement that moved it: running one module from the same cable that flashes the board.

67 V absolute, 75 V for a 10 ms transient at 25 C. The fitted SMCJ40CA reaches 67 V only at 27 A of surge, against 16.5 A for the 60 V TPS54360B and SS36 on the same node, so this part still has the most margin of the three - which sit at 1.03x and are now the binding parts.

DESIGN VALUES, per channel: R_ILIM 3.24 kOhm (5.56 A, from the datasheet's 3k->6A / 4.02k->4.5A table, i.e. I*R ~ 18 kOhm.A), C_dVdT 220 nF, C_IN and C_OUT 220 nF each (p.6 gives 0.1 uF as a MINIMUM), UVLO/OVP string 732k/255k/30.0k (UVLO 4.28 V, OVP 40.68 V against 1.2 V references), SHDN 10 kOhm pull-down with 1 kOhm in series from the GPIO, PGOOD 10 kOhm pull-up shared.

dV/dt COMES FROM EQUATIONS 1 AND 2, NOT FROM THE WORKED EXAMPLE. t(dVdT) = 20.8e3 x V_IN x C_dVdT and I(INRUSH) = C_OUT x V_IN / t(dVdT), i.e. a gain of 1/(20.8e3 x 2 uA) = 24.0, and the datasheet states GAIN(dVdT) = 23.5/25/26 V/V directly on p.7. Back-solving 33x from the rounded example in 10.2.2.3 is wrong by 37%: at 220 nF the ramp is 165 ms and the inrush 0.72 A, not 120 ms and 0.99 A.
DIVIDER TAP ORDER: IN -> R1 -> UVLO -> R2 -> OVP -> R3 -> GND. UVLO is the UPPER tap. Swapping the two pins would put 40.7 V on UVLO and 4.3 V on OVP, i.e. a part that never turns on.

RAMPING 3.3 mF IS CHARACTERISED, NOT INFERRED. TI publishes the part powering into 15 mF (Figure 16, Thermal Regulation Loop Response During Power up with Large Capacitive Load) and it regulates its own junction temperature during start-up. This is the question that cost four review rounds on the discrete P-FET.

COST: 45 mOhm max integrated against 9.5 mOhm discrete plus a 10 mOhm shunt, so 0.53 W of conduction for the pair against 0.23 W, and 0.66 W against 0.35 W once each controller's quiescent and divider draw is carried, and 1.7 mA IQ each. Thermal headroom falls from 1.29x to 1.19x. The PowerPAD must be soldered to a pour with vias - it is the thermal path the regulation loop depends on.

VARIANT CHOICE: TPS16632 adds adjustable output power limiting but fixes the overvoltage clamp, and the binding figure is its 35.7 V MINIMUM (36.6 typ, 39 max, p.7) - the worst-case part clamps below the 36 V nominal bus. Reading the 39 V maximum is the trap: it is the forgiving end and 3.3 V from the number that decides it. The -30 with adjustable OVP cut-off is the right one here.

MODE pin selects latch-off versus auto-retry (p.24 Table 1: open = latch, GND = auto-retry). DECIDED: leave OPEN, i.e. latch off. Firmware already owns SHDN and reads PGOOD, so it can retry with back-off and report; auto-retry would re-pulse 13 W per channel blindly into an already-hot board. Reset by toggling SHDN.
IMON gives a per-channel current monitor, which is exactly what the shared low-side shunt cannot provide. Unused because there are no spare ADC pins; worth revisiting if the GPIO budget loosens.

OVP REFERENCE IS +/-2% (1.176/1.2/1.224 V), not the +/-10% the LM5069 comparator had. That is what lets a 40.68 V trip sit between the 37.8 V maximum bus and the modules' 45 V absolute - with 1% resistors the trip lands 39.1-42.3 V. The 'OVLO cannot protect the modules' limit this design carried for several rounds was inherited from the looser part and does not apply here.

TWO MANDATORY CONNECTIONS beyond the obvious: P_IN (pin 6) must connect to IN directly (p.4), and pin 9 GND must be wired IN ADDITION to the PowerPAD - p.5 says outright not to use the pad as the only ground connection.

SHDN IS A LOGIC INPUT, 0-5 V with V(SHUTR) <= 2 V, driven directly by a 3.3 V GPIO through 1 kOhm with a 10 kOhm pull-down for fail-safe. An earlier design put an open-drain FET on it as well, which gave two paths to ground and none to 3V3 - both channels would have been latched in shutdown. 100 kOhm is also too weak: against the pin's own <=10 uA source it settles near 0.77 V, under the 0.8 V guaranteed-shutdown threshold.

FLT (pin 15) is unconnected. PGOOD goes low for a fault AND for a commanded shutdown, and the two PGOODs are wire-ORed, so the one bit firmware sees is ambiguous twice over. Per-channel FLT would cost two GPIOs the budget does not have. I(SCP) fast-trip is 45 A; turn-on delay is 742 us + 49.5 x C_dVdT[nF] = 11.6 ms.

CONSTANT INRUSH IS THE REAL WIN. Equations 1 and 2 have no V_IN term in the current, so 0.72 A holds at 5 V as at 36 V and both channels can be released together (1.44 A against a 5 A contract). Ramp time has no C_OUT term either - 165 ms at 10 or 20 modules - BUT that is a 25 C figure: Eq. 3 puts the inrush power at 13 W per channel, and above the Figure 13 boundary the thermal regulation loop overrides the slew and starts a 1.1 s minimum (1.25 typ) timeout. At 45 C ambient regulation will engage.

THE OVP RELEASE THRESHOLD STRADDLES THE MAXIMUM BUS. V(OVPF) 1.09/1.122/1.15 V puts recovery at 37.0-39.0 V on the comparator spread and 36.2-39.7 V with 1% resistors, against a compliant source that may sit at 37.8 V indefinitely. A low-corner part that trips would not re-enable on a healthy bus. Raising the trip raises the release with it, so the recovery path is a firmware PD renegotiation down to a lower fixed PDO and back. NOT cycling SHDN: OVP is a hysteretic comparator with its own rising and falling thresholds, and the datasheet's latch-reset sentence belongs to the overload and thermal class, so toggling SHDN above the release point re-enters shutdown in 11 us.

FIGURE 16'S 15 mF IS AT 24 V WITH dVdT OPEN, i.e. 4.32 J. Ours is 2.14 J at 3.3 mF and 36 V, so 2.0x inside TI's demonstrated case rather than the 4x a capacitance comparison suggests - and 1.0x at the 20-module growth case. The thermal loop responds to energy and power, not farads.

§11.1 TRANSIENT PROTECTION (p.28) applies here and is easy to miss: interrupting current makes the output inductance drive OUT negative, against a -0.3 V absolute maximum. The prescribed Schottky from OUT to GND is D15/D16 (MBRS3100T3G, C12790). The same page's Recommended Operating Conditions give 0.1 uF as the minimum capacitance at OUT as well as IN - that is C34/C35.

rules.note: datasheet p.5 Pin Functions: 'Always connect P_IN to IN directly'. P_IN is the sense tap for the internal FET; leaving it off IN makes the current limit read nothing.

datasheet p.6 Recommended Operating Conditions: 0.1 uF MINIMUM external capacitance at IN, P_IN and OUT. Fitted as C3/C4 at 220 nF 100 V - oversized on purpose, because a nominal 100 nF +/-10% part meets a minimum with zero margin.
datasheet p.5 Pin Functions: 'Do not use PowerPad as the only electrical connection to GND'. The GND pin is wired as well as the pad.
floating SHDN is undefined. R13/R14 pull it down so reset is the off state; the GPIO drives it through R11/R12.

datasheet p.6 Recommended Operating Conditions: 0.1 uF minimum external capacitance at IN, P_IN AND OUT. P2-no-decoupling only inspects power_in pins, so this rule is the only thing that can check the output side.
